The highest-transfer analogue (0.8157) shows only 24% brain penetration relative to plasma in rat, making it the strongest individual anchor because it combines the highest transfer score with a direct systemic brain-penetration measurement. Its structure contains an ionizable piperidine and several polar functionalities but is not an obvious extreme BBB non-penetrant. The pattern continues at 0.7708 and 0.7603, where biodistribution and brain-to-blood measurements again show poor CNS exposure. Both molecules retain substantial hydrophobic/aromatic character, demonstrating experimentally that lipophilicity alone does not ensure brain penetration when other liabilities such as ionization, polarity, size, or transporter recognition intervene. - Do not narrate schema bookkeeping.
- Do not analyze the SMILES structure beyond what is obvious.
- Do not override the transfer score of the evidence unless you have very strong reasons to.

Return one or more concise claims, using as many as needed to represent the experimental evidence that materially informs the decision.
